confidence_notes: Restaurant and drink anchors come from three web searches: the RBA rate, Lima cost-of-living indexes (Expat Arrivals, MyLifeElsewhere, Traveltables) and cocktail/wine pages. The index figures differ in year and method, so these anchors are rounded blends. Beer is set slightly above the index figure of about USD 2.1-2.5, because a restaurant serving costs more than a shop or index price. The mid-range meal is set above the Expat Arrivals figure of PEN 100 (about USD 28) to reflect tourist-area restaurants. Cocktail is set below the Expatistan estimate of USD 10, which is a self-described guess from 8 price points, and well below the Miraflores bar and lounge figures of USD 11-12. It is a typical casual-bar price of about 3x beer. Wine by the glass had no reliable Lima average, only one single-menu data point of USD 7, so it is set at about 2x beer. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Lima (tourist districts like Miraflores and Barranco), not from searches or live listings, and are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Lima's own index prices, cross-checked against the typical price relationships in other Andean and Latin American capital cities such as Bogota and Quito. Lima is somewhat pricier than the Peruvian average, especially in Miraflores, San Isidro and Barranco.
